draft.body:
Dear Yoshiyuki Kawazoe,

Your [lab’s community-development approach](https://arch.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/laboratory/kawazoe-lab/) starts with the cultural and environmental relationships of a place.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for people. I want to begin a civic-room pilot by observing how residents arrive, linger and return, before adding any proxy booking or robot. A useful comparison would show whether a new help point supports those relationships or merely shortens a transaction.

Could you comment on an initial fieldwork protocol and whether that architectural question could fit doctoral research in your group?

Best wishes,
Kris Haamer

draft.body:
Dear Yusuke Obuchi,

Your [human-centred fabrication research](https://arch.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/laboratory/obuchi-lab-g30/), including sound-guided PAFF, interests me because people remain active interpreters of spatial instructions.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for people. My prototype would let visitors assemble and alter a small library threshold whose physical indicators show a proxy’s task, expiry and human return. I would compare printed instructions, fixed automation and staged AI guidance, recording misunderstandings as design evidence.

Would you discuss a feasible full-scale fabrication exercise and clarify whether doctoral supervision is possible through your current programme?

Best wishes,
Kris Haamer

Your [lab’s public-space observations and Moriguchi City Library example](https://arch.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/laboratory/yasuhara-lab/) connect design with changing social demands.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for people. Dear Yuji Matsuda,
